unspecified_scores.reason: Every Ask on a .loft reads the small local .loft file once more for the Type line (file_question.py:419 -> _type_label:252) while the read session is open; the user sees nothing beyond a negligible extra read, and the label is correct.
An indexed row with an empty or NULL file_path only arises from hand-edited or corrupt data; the user would just see no Folder line (file_question.py:228-229), which is harmless.

A drive configured with mount '/' is not an ordinary Litloft setup; if it were, the Folder line would carry the full directory without its leading slash (commonpath gives '/', relpath at file_question.py:244), which is still the folder inside that drive, so the effect is minor.

specification_compliance: The three touch-point findings were confirmed from r1/test-files.txt and the files on disk: new test helpers, golden files and test modules lie outside the spec's Touch points list. They are documentation gaps, not invariant breaks.

_folder_in_drive (file_question.py:221-245) checks inclusion by whole segments with os.path.commonpath after normpath, so a sibling prefix mount is excluded and a trailing slash on the mount changes nothing, which matches I2 as read.
